clue.text: Under the influence of spirits, speed so recklessly around a couple of bends

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are wrapped around the pair of bends
driving recklessly throws things about, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

parts.note: an S-bend is a double bend in a road, so two bends give two S letters

explanation.surface: A warning about a driver going too fast through a double bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under the influence of spirits' suggests drink, but here it means taken over by evil spirits. 'recklessly' is the anagram signal and 'around' wraps the jumble round two S-bends.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone possessed is controlled by a demon or ghost that has entered them.

clue.text: Second-guess spin doctors' decree?

parts.note: PR, public relations, is the work of spin doctors
an edict is a decree

explanation.surface: Doubting an order issued by press officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second-guess' usually means doubt after the event; here it means guess beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: To forecast what will happen.

clue.text: Fellow's given pound in which poor boxes? If it's this fellow, none!

definitions.text: Fellow's given pound in which poor boxes? If it's this fellow, none!

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the word for poor goes round the other pieces

parts.note: skint is British slang for having no money
F is the abbreviation for fellow
L is the pound sign, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A charity collection box into which a miser puts nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which poor boxes' means the word for poor (British slang for broke) encloses the other pieces. A poor box is a church charity box, and the whole clue describes a miser.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser who gives nothing to charity.

clue.text: Port's not opened for part-time swimmers

indicators.note: not opened means the first letter is removed

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship, so ports are lefts

explanation.surface: Port wine left unopened, and some occasional swimmers.
explanation.walkthrough: These young newts live on land for part of their life, so they only swim part of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Young newts, which spend a land phase before going back to the water.

clue.text: You are speaking in Spanish, the year after heading for Seville, with confidence

indicators.note: after places the other pieces after the first letter of Seville
the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: UR is how 'you are' sounds when spoken, as in text-speak
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A traveller speaking Spanish confidently a year after reaching Seville.
explanation.walkthrough: S from Seville comes first, as 'after' says; 'You are' said aloud sounds like the letters U and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Surely is said to show certainty, meaning confidently or without doubt.

clue.text: Stop and help up the old man, supported by his offspring

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by puts the next piece beneath
in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: aid means help
pa is father, the old man
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Someone helping an elderly father, who leans on his son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' seems a command but is an organ stop, a set of pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: A principal organ stop, one of the main sets of pipes.

clue.text: Turn up, not having left in time

indicators.note: not having signals that a letter is dropped from the word for time

parts.note: to clock a runner is to time them

explanation.surface: Someone failing to arrive on schedule because they never set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' reads as arriving; it means tilt upward, as a dog does its ears.
explanation.definitionFit: To cock a hat brim or an ear is to tilt it upwards.

clue.text: Am I always unable to cross lake with this sort of bridge?

indicators.note: to cross here means to sit across, so the lake goes inside the rest

parts.note: can't means unable
ever means always

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether they can ever get over a lake with a certain bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Am I always unable' is read as 'Can't I ever', with 'Am' a link; 'to cross' puts L inside CANTIEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridge type built from arms anchored at one end, projecting over the gap.

clue.text: He explored Virginia, for instance, going north and avoiding Colorado

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means read upwards, backwards
avoiding means leaving out the abbreviation for Colorado

parts.note: Virginia is a type of tobacco
CO is the US state abbreviation for Colorado

explanation.surface: An explorer travelling up through Virginia, bypassing Colorado.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' takes CO from TOBACCO, leaving TOBAC, which 'going north' turns to CABOT. Virginia looks like the state but is the tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cabot was the Venetian navigator who reached North America in 1497.

clue.text: Diver has to do this exercise involving breathing apparatus

indicators.note: involving means containing, so exercise surrounds the organ

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
a lung is the organ we breathe with

explanation.surface: A diver doing a training drill with breathing gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breathing apparatus' suggests scuba gear but is the body's own lung.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver's leap into water is a dive downward.

clue.text: European champion producing a letter giving notice?

definitions.note: the definition describes a person, one producing such a letter

parts.note: the victor is the winner, the champion

explanation.surface: A European title-holder writing a formal letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of a person: one who sends a notice to quit, typically a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord removing a tenant serves written notice to quit first.

clue.text: She makes an arrest and finishes off police patrol

parts.note: to nab a suspect is to arrest them

indicators.note: the finishes of the two words are their final letters

explanation.surface: A woman police officer making an arrest at the end of her beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishes off' takes the last letters of 'police' and 'patrol', E and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so any woman bearing it could be called she.

clue.text: Partaking of spliff -yes, that's risky

indicators.note: Partaking of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone agreeing to share a joint while admitting it is a dubious idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for dodgy or uncertain, describing something of doubtful safety.

clue.text: Shabby female, skinny, imbibes beer endlessly

indicators.note: imbibes means drinks in, so the beer goes inside the word for skinny

parts.note: skinny means lean

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the beer is cut off

parts.note: bitter is a British style of draught beer

explanation.surface: A thin, scruffy woman drinking beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final R of the beer and 'imbibes' places what is left inside the word for skinny. Bitter is a British pub beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally bitten by fleas, it is used loosely for worn and scruffy.

clue.text: I missed out, so Prague tour ultimately is awful?

definitions.text: I missed out, so Prague tour ultimately is awful?

indicators.note: awful here signals the letters are put into a messy new order
ultimately takes the last letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone who missed a trip insisting the trip was bad anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives R and S from 'tour' and 'is'. The whole clue is an example of the attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Belittling something only because you could not have it, as in Aesop's fox.

clue.text: Trumpeter's case-something that can store music stand

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: an iPod is Apple's portable music player

explanation.surface: A trumpeter's case containing a gadget for keeping music, and a music stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' takes the first and last letters of 'Trumpeter's', T and R. 'music stand' looks like one item, but 'music' ends the iPod description and 'stand' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged support, such as one for a camera.

clue.text: Check motorway speed traps round outskirts of Dunstable

indicators.note: traps means holds inside, so the motorway and speed letters enclose the rest

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
rate means speed
O is round in shape

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Police checking speeds on a motorway near Dunstable, a town in Bedfordshire, England.
explanation.walkthrough: Dunstable is a town in Bedfordshire; 'outskirts of' takes its first and last letters, and 'traps' sets them, with O, between the motorway and speed pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate something is to restrain or curb it.

clue.text: A timeless human condition — lacking sense of right and wrong

definitions.text: lacking sense of right and wrong
definitions.note: an adjective phrase defining a noun: the state of lacking such sense

indicators.note: timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: mortality, being bound to die, is the human condition

explanation.surface: A philosophical remark that humans have always lacked moral sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' removes T, the abbreviation for time, from MORTALITY.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of having no moral principles at all.

clue.text: Short stay became hard for ancient settler

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a visit is a short stay
got means became, as in got angry
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A brief stop that grew tough for an early settler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts VISIT to VISI.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the western Gothic people who settled in Spain and Gaul.

clue.text: I cut girl out of act of worship

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cutting a girl from a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a set form of public church service.

clue.text: What's left on account's unknown

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
AC is the abbreviation for account
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A bank balance described as unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's left' means bequeathed in a will. The on side in cricket is the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest, something handed down in a will.

clue.text: The Iron Lady's capital investment?

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Dora is a woman's name, standing for a lady

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher, the Iron Lady, putting money into a venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Iron Lady' points at Thatcher, but splits into iron and lady. 'capital' means head, so a capital investment is something put on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft felt brimmed hat, something worn on the head.

clue.text: Jack needs to do a crossword — that's clear

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB, able seaman, is too
to solve a puzzle is to do it

explanation.surface: A man named Jack needing to do a puzzle, which is plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear' looks like 'that's obvious' but means free from blame.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to pardon, freeing someone of guilt.

clue.text: Sophoclean character appears twice as pretentious

indicators.note: appears twice means the letter is written two times in a row

parts.note: Sophocles wrote in Greek, so a character of his is a Greek letter, chi

explanation.surface: A figure in a Greek tragedy appearing twice and being showy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' suggests a role in a play but means a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Affectedly fashionable or showy.

clue.text: Finally rejecting old way, start to act bound by morality?

definitions.text: Finally rejecting old way, start to act bound by morality?

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: bound by means held inside, so the start of act sits within the word for morality

parts.note: right is what is morally good

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone giving up a former life of crime to behave morally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to act' gives A, which 'bound by' places inside RIGHT; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to give up crime and live honestly, as the clue describes.

clue.text: Half-heartedly mounts soap dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounts means climbs, so the word is read upwards
half-heartedly means one of the two central letters is dropped

parts.note: Dallas was a long-running American TV soap opera

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly staging a soap opera about food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-heartedly' drops one L from DALLAS, leaving DALAS, which 'mounts' turns upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold dish of mixed raw vegetables or leaves.

clue.text: Approval's needed to import American trees

indicators.note: to import means to bring in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: OK is approval, so OK's in the plural or possessive gives OKS

explanation.surface: Approval required for bringing in trees from the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad trees bearing acorns.

clue.text: Two knights arise, offering weapon

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for knight

indicators.note: in a down clue, arise means the word goes upward, read backwards

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: Two knights rising to give a sword, as at a dubbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arise' recalls 'Arise, Sir Knight' at a dubbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Malay dagger with a wavy blade.

clue.text: Charlie too entertains nymph regularly-this one?

definitions.text: Charlie too entertains nymph regularly-this one?

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold within, so the picked letters go inside

parts.note: also means too

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man named Charlie also hosting a nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes every other letter of nymph and 'entertains' places them inside the other pieces. 'this one' points back to the nymph: she is the nymph who held Odysseus on her island.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Odyssey she is the sea nymph who kept Odysseus captive for seven years.

clue.text: Friendly company gets Regina relaxed?

parts.note: R stands for Regina, Latin for queen, as in a royal cipher
relaxed is laid back, read cryptically as laid written backwards

explanation.surface: A business persuading a woman named Regina to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxed?' means laid back, and the question mark admits that this is to be read as the word laid turned back.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm and amicable in manner, as in cordial relations.

clue.text: Backsliding Democratic Party needs second advantage

indicators.note: backsliding means going backwards, so the two pieces together are read in reverse

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A political party slipping back and needing a second chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Democratic Party' looks like one name, but gives D and DO; 'Backsliding' turns D plus DO into ODD.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds can mean an advantage given, as a head start or handicap.

clue.text: DA, for one, could get hysterical when caught out

indicators.note: could get signals that the letters can be rearranged into something new
out means the letter for caught must be left out of the jumble

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A district attorney, DA, becoming hysterical when caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'DA' looks like a district attorney but is a duck's arse, a 1950s swept-back haircut. Remove C from HYSTERICAL and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck's arse is a quiffed men's cut, so it is an example of a way of doing hair.
